/glossary/thermal-radiation.title: Thermal Radiation — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/thermal-radiation.metaDesc: The intense pulse of light and infrared radiation emitted by the fireball of a nuclear detonation, capable of causing burns and igniting fires at long distances.

/glossary/fallout.title: Fallout — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/fallout.metaDesc: Radioactive material thrown into the atmosphere by a surface-burst nuclear detonation, which then settles back to earth over hours to weeks.

/glossary/air-burst.title: Air Burst — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/air-burst.metaDesc: A nuclear detonation above the ground at optimal altitude, maximizing the area affected by blast and thermal radiation while producing minimal fallout.

/glossary/teller-ulam.title: Teller-Ulam Design — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/teller-ulam.metaDesc: The two-stage design used in nearly all modern thermonuclear weapons, named after physicists Edward Teller and Stanislaw Ulam.

/glossary/emp.title: EMP (Electromagnetic Pulse) — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/emp.metaDesc: A burst of electromagnetic energy released by a nuclear detonation, capable of damaging or destroying unhardened electronics over a wide area.

/glossary/acute-radiation-syndrome.title: Acute Radiation Syndrome — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/acute-radiation-syndrome.metaDesc: The constellation of medical symptoms following a high dose of ionizing radiation, including nausea, immune-system failure, hemorrhage, and death.

/glossary/atomic-bomb.title: Atomic Bomb — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/atomic-bomb.metaDesc: A nuclear weapon whose energy comes from nuclear fission of uranium-235 or plutonium-239.

/glossary/surface-burst.title: Surface Burst — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/surface-burst.metaDesc: A nuclear detonation at ground level, producing roughly 40-50% smaller blast radius than an air burst but creating massive radioactive fallout.

/glossary/nuclear-winter.title: Nuclear Winter — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/nuclear-winter.metaDesc: A hypothesized severe global cooling caused by soot from urban firestorms following a large-scale nuclear war.

/glossary/thermonuclear-weapon.title: Thermonuclear Weapon — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/thermonuclear-weapon.metaDesc: Synonym for hydrogen bomb — a nuclear weapon whose primary energy comes from fusion reactions.

/glossary/hydrogen-bomb.title: Hydrogen Bomb — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/hydrogen-bomb.metaDesc: A nuclear weapon that derives most of its energy from nuclear fusion of hydrogen isotopes, ignited by a fission primary stage.

/glossary/warhead.title: Warhead — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/warhead.metaDesc: The explosive payload of a missile, bomb, or other weapon system; for nuclear weapons, the package containing the fissile or fusion material.

/glossary/tactical-nuclear-weapon.title: Tactical Nuclear Weapon — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/tactical-nuclear-weapon.metaDesc: A nuclear weapon designed for battlefield use, typically with low yield (sub-kiloton to ~50 kilotons) and short range.

/glossary/cruise-missile.title: Cruise Missile — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/cruise-missile.metaDesc: A self-propelled jet- or rocket-powered missile that flies a low, terrain-following trajectory to a target.

/glossary/icbm.title: ICBM (Intercontinental Ballistic Missile) — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/icbm.metaDesc: A long-range ballistic missile (range > 5,500 km) designed to deliver nuclear warheads between continents.

/glossary/strategic-nuclear-weapon.title: Strategic Nuclear Weapon — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/strategic-nuclear-weapon.metaDesc: A nuclear weapon designed for long-range strikes against an adversary's population centers, industrial base, or strategic infrastructure.

/glossary/kiloton.title: Kiloton (kt) — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/kiloton.metaDesc: A unit of nuclear yield equal to 1,000 tons of TNT equivalent (4.184 × 10¹² joules).

/glossary/neutron-bomb.title: Neutron Bomb — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/neutron-bomb.metaDesc: A small thermonuclear weapon designed to maximize neutron radiation output relative to blast and thermal effects.

/glossary/mirv.title: MIRV — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/mirv.metaDesc: Multiple Independently-targetable Reentry Vehicle — a single missile carrying several warheads, each able to strike a different target.

/glossary/slbm.title: SLBM (Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missile) — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/slbm.metaDesc: A ballistic missile launched from a submerged submarine, providing a survivable second-strike nuclear capability.

/glossary/yield.title: Yield — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/yield.metaDesc: The total energy released by a nuclear weapon, expressed in tons (or kilotons / megatons) of TNT equivalent.

/glossary/nuclear-fission.title: Nuclear Fission — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/nuclear-fission.metaDesc: The splitting of heavy atomic nuclei (typically uranium-235 or plutonium-239) into lighter fragments, releasing large amounts of energy.

/glossary/nuclear-fusion.title: Nuclear Fusion — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/nuclear-fusion.metaDesc: The combination of light atomic nuclei (typically deuterium and tritium) into heavier nuclei, releasing energy.

/glossary/megaton.title: Megaton (Mt) — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/megaton.metaDesc: A unit of nuclear yield equal to 1,000,000 tons (or 1,000 kilotons) of TNT equivalent.

/glossary/deuterium.title: Deuterium — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/deuterium.metaDesc: A heavy isotope of hydrogen with one neutron, used as fusion fuel in thermonuclear weapons.

/glossary/half-life.title: Half-Life — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/half-life.metaDesc: The time required for half of a quantity of a radioactive isotope to decay.

/glossary/critical-mass.title: Critical Mass — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/critical-mass.metaDesc: The minimum amount of fissile material required to sustain a self-propagating nuclear chain reaction.

/glossary/tritium.title: Tritium — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/tritium.metaDesc: A radioactive heavy isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons, used as fusion fuel and in boosted-fission weapons.

/glossary/sievert.title: Sievert (Sv) — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/sievert.metaDesc: The SI unit of equivalent dose of ionizing radiation, accounting for biological effect.

/glossary/plutonium-239.title: Plutonium-239 — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/plutonium-239.metaDesc: A fissile isotope of plutonium produced from uranium-238 in nuclear reactors and used in most modern fission weapons.

/glossary/mad.title: MAD (Mutually Assured Destruction) — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/mad.metaDesc: A Cold War strategic doctrine in which two or more nuclear-armed adversaries each possess sufficient retaliatory capability that any nuclear attack would result in their own destruction.

/glossary/second-degree-burns.title: Second-Degree Burns — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/second-degree-burns.metaDesc: Partial-thickness burns affecting both the epidermis and dermis, characterized by blistering and pain.

/glossary/uranium-235.title: Uranium-235 — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/uranium-235.metaDesc: A fissile isotope of uranium that constitutes the explosive material in many fission weapons.

/glossary/gamma-radiation.title: Gamma Radiation — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/gamma-radiation.metaDesc: High-energy electromagnetic radiation emitted by nuclear processes, capable of penetrating most materials and damaging living tissue.

/glossary/boosted-fission.title: Boosted Fission — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/boosted-fission.metaDesc: A fission weapon design in which a small amount of deuterium-tritium gas is injected into the fissile core to enhance yield.

/glossary/first-strike.title: First Strike — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/first-strike.metaDesc: A nuclear attack intended to disarm an opponent before they can retaliate, by destroying their nuclear forces, command, and control.

/glossary/second-strike.title: Second Strike — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
/glossary/second-strike.metaDesc: The retaliatory nuclear capability remaining after absorbing an opponent's first strike — the foundation of deterrence under MAD.

/glossary/nuclear-triad.title: Nuclear Triad — Nuclear Weapons Glossary | NukeBlastSimulator.com
